title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks with same price increase saw sales drop to 10 and 7 units (vs baseline 7.7), suggesting demand elasticity. Past promotions show weak response to price changes; noise-adjusted promotion lift is only x1.16.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.7. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased 2.3% to $9.03, above regular $8.83. Past price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 10 and 7 units—below baseline—suggesting price sensitivity. The 30% off promotion in Apr 2026 lifted sales to x2.86, but the 10% off promotions had smaller lifts (x1.03–x1.11). The noise-adjusted estimate for promotions is only x1.16, indicating weak average lift. With no promotion planned and a price increase, the effect is likely negative. The classical model suggests no uplift, but it ignores price. A 2.3% price hike with weak past promotion response implies a modest demand drop. The median multiplier is adjusted downward, with moderate confidence due to limited evidence.

  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.7 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 33.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 21.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
